## Natural history notes

A medium-sized tussock moth characterized by gray to brownish forewings with subtle darker markings and a fuzzy-bodied appearance, while the caterpillars are hairy with distinctive tufts typical of tussock moths. In Florida, the Southern Tussock Moth is found in wooded and semi-wooded habitats such as hammocks, pine flatwoods, forest edges, parks, and yards where suitable tree and shrub hosts occur. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars feed on foliage and should be handled cautiously because tussock moth hairs can irritate skin.
